subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Solar Panels: Photons to Electrons
description: One-minute skill: Solar Panels: Photons to Electrons.

hook.text: A solar panel has no moving parts. Sunlight hits silicon and electrons start flowing. Pure solid-state magic.

buildup.text: Photons knock electrons loose in the silicon. A built-in electric field at the P-N junction sweeps them into a circuit.

discovery.text: Bell Labs made the first practical solar cell in 1954. It converted 6% of sunlight to electricity.

twist.text: Modern panels exceed 22% efficiency. Perovskite cells in labs reach 33%. Costs dropped 99% since 1976.

climax.text: Solar is now the cheapest electricity source in most countries. It's cheaper than running existing coal plants.

punchline.text: Light hits silicon. Electrons flow. No combustion needed.

quiz.question: How have solar panel costs changed since 1976?
options: They dropped about 50%, making them competitive with gas
They dropped 99%, making solar the cheapest source in most countries
They stayed roughly the same but efficiency gains offset costs
